previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing multiple tonic-clonic seizures, the most recent occurring at home during a flare of chronic pancreatitis. Initial evaluation revealed no acute intracranial abnormalities on CT or MRI, but prior EEG showed left temporal lobe slowing, supporting a diagnosis of temporal lobe epilepsy. Seizures were likely provoked by polypharmacy, including tramadol and benzodiazepines, along with sleep deprivation and pain. She was started on levetiracetam and remained seizure-free during admission. Chronic pancreatitis was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV analgesia, transitioning to oral pain control. A multidisciplinary plan was established to address medication overuse, including a pain contract, disposal of excess medications, and enrollment in a partial psychiatric program. She was discharged home with services, on a limited tramadol and lorazepam regimen, and follow-up arranged with neurology, PCP, and mental health specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ F w/ chronic pancreatitis, polydrug abuse, and multiple 
hospitalizations for abdominal pain p/w with epigastric pain 
which she describes as her typical pancreatitis symptoms. 
.
# CHRONIC PANCREATITIS: presented with classic symptom of 
epigastric pain radiating to back. AST/ALT and lipase were 
normal during admission. She was started on her usual 
pancreatitis treatment protocol established at prior admissions. 
 
-- NPO except meds  
-- Normal saline at 100 ml/hr  
-- Dilaudid 2 mg IV Q3H:PRN pain  
-- Dilute Dilaudid in NS 50 ml and infuse over 15 minutes. 
-- Ketorolac 30 mg IV Q8H for 3 Days  
-- Promethazine 25 mg IV Q6H:PRN nausea  
-- Lorazepam 1 mg IV Q4H:PRN nausea or anxiety  
-- Lorazepam 1 mg IV HS:PRN insomnia  
On ___, femoral line was removed, patient was transitioned 
to po dilaudid, and then to outpatient dose of tramadol. At 
discharge, she was weaned off po dilaudid and sent home with 
increased dose of tramadol, promethazine, ativan as per PCP 
___ (please see below under transitional issue). She 
also reported improvement of her pain and was able to tolerate 
all her meals. 
.
# UTI- UA positive and growing E. coli sensitive to cipro. She 
was started with cipro and will complete a 7 day course.   
.
# Drug abuse: patient with long history of drug abuse including 
benzos, tramadol, seroquel, fioricet, methadone. Last admission 
with extensive conversations with PCP (Dr. ___, SW, 
psych regarding future treatment. Plan is to have all pain 
medications to be prescribed only by PCP, attend an outpatient 
partial day psych program at ___, and close follow up with 
PCP, ___, pain/GI/psych doctors. 
.
# HTN: patient with elevated BPs up to 200s/100s and lisinopril 
was increased from 10 mg to 30mg daily. Despite increase, she 
had occasional elevated BPs up to 170s that usually occurred 
after emesis or period of stress (especially after conversations 
regarding changes in her pain meds). Elevated BP usually 
normalizes after treatment of pain. 
.
# CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Migraine headache: stable, on acetaminophen-Caff-Butalbital 
PRN. Attempted to minimize use of this medication due to prior 
history of abuse. 
# Depression: continued on home Amitriptyline, Mirtazapine, 
Sertraline

area making patient prone to seizures. Continued with 
levetiracetam
# GERD- continued with omeprazole 
.

plan to switch her seizure medication from keppra to lamictal 
-patient missed her intake for outpatient psych program at ___ 
___ due to need for hospitalization. Please check that patient 
has rescheduled her appointment
.

peripheral line, po meds, J tube, or IM/PR if necessary.
